messages:
alex: Heads-up: we just saw another OOM clusterwide during the 22:00 deploy window. Pattern looks like long-running KV shard residency growth + slab fragmentation. Crash log attached in vault, but gist of it: frequent tiny allocs + large slow-to-evict entries.
priya: ugh. Is this the same workload that previous postmortem called out? (the one with prefix-hits growth)
dan: yes, appears correlated with the feature flag 'session-indexing'. When traffic is high we see a slow but steady increase in KV residency on shards 7-12. GC runs but doesn't reclaim due to many pinned small objects.
megan: can someone dump a pprof or heap snapshot from a live box? need to confirm whether it's fragmentation vs true leak.
alex: on it — spinning a profiling job on one node now. command: ```./tools/profiler --node node-7 --duration 10m --out /tmp/heap-3512349999.pb```
joel: re: quick mitigation, we can enable the temporary soft-eviction gate we used last month. That will aggressively evict entries older than 24h even if residency looks recent. Needs a short canary though.
priya: assign owners: alex for profiling and heap export, dan for root-cause triage on the session-indexing path, megan for GC policy tuning proposal, joel for mitigation rollout plan. When are we aiming to have mitigations live?
alex: profile done — uploaded to stash at s3://redwood-profiles/3512349999/heap.pb. Initial quick look: lots of 64B allocations from session-indexing encode step, and a hotlist of objects never referenced by LRU because we use a non-global LRU in that codepath.
megan: that sounds like fragmentation + logical leak (objects not tracked for eviction). Proposed immediate changes: 1) lower slab bucket for 64B to prefer pooling, 2) enable extra compaction GC pass every 5m for 30m after spikes, 3) add eviction watermark at 70% residency. Thoughts?
dan: Agree on 1 and 3. For 2 worried about compaction run CPU cost — but acceptable as short-term canary. Need to add metrics to measure compaction CPU and reclaimed bytes.
joel: rollout plan: canary 2 nodes in us-west, enable soft-eviction + compaction pass. Monitor: p95 latency, eviction-rate, OOM events. If stable 6h, roll to us-east, then rest. Rollback toggle: disable soft-eviction and revert GC pass.
alex: created issue #INF-9843 with logs + heap. Linking here: <https://issues.redwood.ai/INF-9843>
priya: timeline and action items: - alex: deep heap diff and write short repro steps (due in 6h) - dan: audit session-indexing references and add missing LRU bookkeeping (due EOD) - megan: implement compaction config and metrics (PR in 8h) - joel: prepare canary infra + runbook (canary ready in 3h) Please update INF-9843 when you start.
megan: quick note on metrics: add `kv.compaction.cpu_ms`, `kv.eviction.reclaimed_bytes`, `kv.residency.percent` to the per-shard dashboard. I'll add them and create an alert for residency >75% for 10m.
dan: repro attempt locally: I could reproduce residency growth with a load generator script that does many short-lived session writes with random keys and occasional large batched updates. Script: ```python
for i in range(200000):
  k = f"sess-{randint(0,1000000)}"
  put(k, small_blob(64))
  if i % 1000 == 0:
    put(bulk_key, large_blob(2048))
```
alex: good. If we can repro, we should add a unit test for housekeeping that ensures small objects get pooled and LRU touched.
joel: operational checklist for canary: - snapshot baseline metrics - enable soft-eviction + compaction - run load test for 2h - monitor OOMs & latency - if p95 latency increase >20% rollback - if no OOMs after 6h progressively roll to 25%/50%/100%
priya: one more recurring pattern note: these OOMs spike when multi-tenant background jobs run concurrently with high write bursts. We should schedule background compactions staggered across shards to avoid concurrent compaction pressure.
megan: I'll add a scheduler patch: stagger compaction by shard-id % 10 and include a max CPU cap. PR will reference INF-9843.
alex: status: heap diff in INF-9843 pushed. Found missing LRU touch in session-indexing when we write with the 'fast-path' encoder. Created a small patch and smoke test.
dan: merged the bookkeeping fix to canary branch. Will monitor canary nodes.
joel: canary started at 3512350800. Monitoring now. sre-bot: Incident note: Canary now running on nodes node-7 and node-9. Alerts bound to residency >75% set to warn. :eyes:
megan: early signal: eviction.reclaimed_bytes up by 3x, compaction CPU ~12% on canary nodes, p95 latency +3%. so far so good.
alex: can we set a tentative postmortem follow-up meeting? Suggest tomorrow 11:00 to review root cause, long-term design (pooling, LRU consolidation), and release plan.
priya: scheduled: calendar invite sent for tomorrow 11:00. Action owners, please add short notes to INF-9843 before the meeting.
joel: if canary holds for 6h, I'll trigger staged rollout. Will post final update here.
sre-bot: Update: Canary passed 6h mark with no OOMs. Will begin staged rollout at 3512354400. :tada:
alex: thanks everyone. Great sprint. Follow-ups: add unit test for pooling (alex), finalize scheduling patch (megan), production rollout doc + rollback playbook (joel).
